title: BDL Basic Circular No. 1: Electronic Payment Services Providers
text:
Basic Circular No. 1
to Electronic Payment Services Providers
Attached is a copy of Basic Decision No. 13790 of 9 January 2026, relating to Electronic
Payment Services Providers.
Beirut, 9 January 2026
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid

Basic Decision No. 13790
Electronic Payment Services Providers
The Governor of the Banque du Liban,
Pursuant to the Code of Money and Credit, in particular Articles 70 and 174 thereof;
Pursuant to Law No. 133 of 26 October 1999 relating to the General Mission of the
Banque du Liban; and
Pursuant to the Decision of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, taken in its
meeting of 7 January 2026,
Decides the following:
Part I
Definitions
Article 1 - Definitions:
For the purposes of this Decision, the following terms shall have the meanings hereunder
assigned to them:
1. Electronic Means: Any tool, system, or technical means used to execute payment
services electronically.
2. Electronic Payment Services: The services specified in Article 2 of this Decision.
3. Electronic Payment Services Provider: Any institution intending to provide any
Electronic Payment Service, except for banks, financial institutions, and exchange
institutions (the Institution).
4. Electronic Know Your Customer (E-KYC) Service: The operations related to
verifying a customer’s identity electronically.
5. E-Money Service: A service for storing funds that represent a specific financial
balance in electronic wallets (E-Wallets).
6. Local Money Transfer Service: A service for sending or receiving funds
electronically within the country via a local network.
7. Cross-border Money Transfer Service: A service for sending or receiving funds
electronically abroad through a contract with a foreign company.
2

8. Money Collection and Payment Service: A service for receiving money and paying
bills and taxes (including university and school fees) in favor of ministries, public
institutions, public administrations, syndicates, mobile and landline telephone
companies, universities, schools, and commercial institutions registered exclusively in
the Commercial Register, with the purpose of re-transferring such funds to these
institutions under the conditions specified in this Decision.
9. Payment Facilitators Services: Services related to e-technologies that facilitate
electronic payments.
10. Payment Gateway Service: A service falling under Payment Facilitators Services,
specifically for collecting electronic payments and disbursing them to beneficiaries.
11. Payment Account: An account opened in the name of a user, that is used exclusively
for executing payments, and that is not considered a deposit account in any form
(including savings account) as per Article 125 of the Code of Money and Credit.
Accordingly, the user shall not benefit from the provisions relating to the National
Deposit Guarantee Institution established under Law No. 28/67 of 9 May 1967.
12. Virtual Assets: A digital representation of a value that is not issued by a Central bank
or a public authority, is not necessarily linked to a legally established currency (Fiat
Currency), but is accepted as a means of exchange and can be transferred, stored, or
traded electronically.
3

Part II
Licensing Requirements for Electronic Payment Services Providers
Article 2 - General Provisions:
1. Any Institution intending to provide any services covered by this Decision must obtain a
prior approval from the Banque du Liban (BDL) in order to be licensed as an Electronic
Payment Services Provider, and thereby provide one or more of the following
categories of services:
Category Service
A E-Money
B Local Money Transfer
C Cross-border Money Transfer
D Money Collection and Payment
E Payment Facilitators
2. The BDL Central Council shall grant the license to the applicant insofar as it deems that it
serves the public interest, after verifying the extent of compliance with the licensing
requirements below, as well as the professional, financial, and moral competence of the
founders, beneficial owners, capital subscribers, and individuals to be entrusted with
senior administrative positions.
3. The BDL shall issue a list of licensed Electronic Payment Services Providers, including
the categories of services they are authorized to provide.
4. After being licensed as Electronic Payment Services Provider, the licensed Institution may
expand its services on condition that:
a- A prior approval from the BDL is obtained for any additional service within the
above-mentioned categories of services. The BDL may classify any service not
mentioned in this Decision under the appropriate category.
b- The minimum capital requirement is increased as per Article 4 below.
c- The feasibility of providing the additional service is demonstrated as well as the ability
to control associated risks.
5. The licensed Institution must display on its website, electronic application, and documents
(where applicable), the number granted to it by the BDL.
4

Article 3 - Legal Form and Bylaws:
1. The licensed Institution must be a Lebanese joint-stock company with nominal shares,
and its shareholding structure must be simplified and clear.
2. The Institution must limit its activities to providing one or more categories of the
services above, and to operations directly related to these services.
3. The Institution must include in its bylaws provisions that require:
a- Obtaining prior approval from the BDL for any:
 Amendment to its bylaws.
 Subscription to, and trading of its shares that would lead to the acquisition
by any individual, whether directly or indirectly, of more than 5% of its
total shares.
b- Refraining from borrowing in any form.
c- Maintaining professional confidentiality and bearing responsibility, towards
third parties, for operations carried out by the Institution, its branches, or its
agents (where applicable).
Article 4 - Minimum Capital Requirement:
1. The Institution must allocate a minimum capital in Lebanese pound for each of the
categories listed in the table below:
Category Minimum Capital Required
A LBP 50 billion, provided that it is not less than USD 558,660
B LBP 50 billion, provided that it is not less than USD 558,660
C LBP 50 billion, provided that it is not less than USD 558,660
D LBP 50 billion, provided that it is not less than USD 558,660
E LBP 25 billion, provided that it is not less than USD 279,330
2. The minimum capital requirements are cumulative according to the number of categories.
3. The capital shall be subscribed to in a single payment at the BDL within a maximum
period of three (3) months from the date of licensing, under penalty of having the
Institution’s license revoked.
4. The capital shall be deposited in a special and separate account specifically opened for
this purpose at the BDL in the name of the concerned institution.
5. Eighty-five percent (85%) of the aforementioned capital shall be released once the legal
documents are duly registered with the competent authorities and a copy thereof
submitted to the BDL.
5

6. The remaining fifteen percent (15%) shall be frozen at the BDL and must not be less than
USD 83,800 for Categories A, B, C, and D, and USD 41,900 for Category E. The
Institution must verify, on a monthly basis, that the funds deposited in Lebanese pound at
the BDL are equivalent to the aforementioned amount in US dollars for the relevant
category. The Institution shall cover any shortfall in Lebanese pound.
7. The aforementioned fifteen percent (15%) shall not be returned to the Institution except
upon the liquidation of its business.
8. The same mechanism specified above shall apply upon any capital increase.
9. The paid-in capital by the shareholders must be sufficient to cover operating expenses for
at least one year.
10. The Institution is prohibited from engaging in any activity before it has obtained the
BDL’s license and its capital is fully subscribed to.
Article 5 - Fit and Proper:
First: The Institution must evidence that:
1. The shareholders, members of the Board of Directors, and senior
management, meet the requirements specified in Annex (1) (where
applicable).
2. The sources of the shareholders’s funds are clear and legitimate.
3. Its recruitment policy and internal control procedures ensure that its
employees, or the persons delegated or appointed to act on its behalf, meet
the conditions specified in Annex (1) (where applicable).
Second: The Central Council is entitled to object to the election of the Chairperson or any
member of the Institution’s Board of Directors, or to the continuation of any of
their terms of office. Objections by the BDL in this regard shall be binding on the
Institution and the concerned shareholders. For this purpose, the Central Council
shall enjoy discretionary power, to be exercised as required by public interest.
Article 6 - Governance:
The Institution must prepare an organizational structure that:
1. Clarifies the identity of the members of the Board of Directors and any other
manager, along with their respective responsibilities.
2. Defines the distribution of the various Departments and Units within the Institution
and how they communicated with the General Manager and/or the Board of Directors.
3. Ensures the separation between supervisory tasks (i.e., risk management, compliance,
and internal audit) and executive tasks, as well as the absence of any conflicts of
interest.
6

Article 7 - Business Plan and Exit Plan:
1. The Institution must prepare a detailed five-year Business Plan in a scientific and
precise manner, that includes at least the following information:
 Business Strategy
 Types of Products and Operations
 Market Share for each service
 Target Market
 Organizational Structure
 Key Risks and Risk Management Approach
 SWOT Analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats)
 Financial Projections, including projections for the expected development of
services to be provided, as well as the projected profit and loss statement.
 Marketing Strategy
 Data Protection
 Strategy for using branches and agents to provide services (where applicable)
2. The Institution must prepare an Exit Plan, particularly if it is unable to achieve its
business objectives. This plan should include the steps to be taken to protect its
customers.
Article 8 - Business Procedures:
The Institution must prepare business procedures for each category of services to be provided
(at the level of the Institution, branches, and agents, where applicable), that include the
following:
1. The internal policies, procedures, and controls related to each category.
2. The customer onboarding process, where applicable, and Multifactor Authentication
Procedures.
3. The suitability of these policies and procedures for the services to be provided.
Article 9 - IT Infrastructure and Information Security Framework:
The Institution must prepare a detailed description (at the level of the Institution, branches,
and agents, where applicable) of its IT infrastructure and information security framework,
which must include, at least, the following:
1. An IT infrastructure plan that covers applications, systems, data centers, networks,
and operations.
2. Information security measures implemented to protect customers' funds, financial and
personal data, and to mitigate operational, fraud, and breach of trust risks.
3. A Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan.
4. Agreements related to outsourcing IT services (where applicable).
7

Article 10 - Risk Management Framework:
1. The Institution must establish a Risk Management Unit or appoint a Risk Officer,
depending on the size and nature of its business.
2. The Institution must prepare a risk management framework (at the level of the
Institution, branches, and agents, where applicable), that is consistent with the
services to be provided and that include, at least, the following:
a- The policies, procedures, systems, and controls necessary for managing the risks
associated with the categories of services to be provided, including those related to
risk identification, monitoring, and mitigation.
b- The human and technical resources to be allocated for risk management.
Article 11 - Compliance Arrangements:
1. The Institution must establish a Compliance Unit or appoint a Compliance Officer,
depending on the size and nature of its business. This Unit must be independent from
the Institution’s daily operations, reporting administratively to the General Manager,
and communicating directly with the Board of Directors.
2. The Institution must prepare a detailed description of the compliance procedures (at
the level of the Institution, branches, and agents, where applicable) that is consistent
with the services to be provided and that include, at least, the following:
a- Policies and procedures that ensure compliance with AML/CFT requirements,
as well as the requirements of this Decision.
b- The role of the Compliance Unit and of the human and technical resources to
be allocated to the Unit.
c- In the absence of a Compliance Unit, the role of the Compliance Officer who
must have sufficient expertise in AML/CFT and undergo continuous training
in this field.
Article 12 - Internal Audit:
1. The Institution must establish an Internal Audit Unit or appoint an Internal Auditor,
depending on the size and nature of its business.
2. The Institution must prepare a detailed description of the internal audit procedures (at
the level of the Institution, branches, and agents), that is consistent with the services
to be provided and that include, at least, the following:
a- The role of the Internal Audit Unit in assessing the adequacy and effectiveness
of the internal control procedures, the compliance with applicable laws and
regulations, the IT infrastructure, the information security, and the human and
technical resources to be allocated to this Unit.
8

b- In the absence of an Internal Audit Unit, the role of the Internal Auditor who
must have sufficient expertise in this field.
Article 13 - Customer Protection:
The Institution must prepare a detailed policy on customer protection procedures (at the level
of the Institution, branches, and agents), that includes at least the following:
1. Measures adopted to protect customers’ funds (where applicable).
2. Measures adopted to protect information privacy.
3. Types of fees and commissions to be applied to the services provided.
4. Customer dispute resolution mechanism and the role of the party in charge of
receiving customers’ claims.
Article 14 - Licensing Documents:
1. The Institution must submit a request in four copies to the BDL, one of which must be
the original, along with the documents specified in Annex (2).
2. The licensing request shall be automatically rejected if it does not include all the
documents specified in Annex (2) and prepared as per the requirements thereof.
Article 15 - Commencement of Operations:
1. The Institution must commence its operations, as per the submitted Business Plan,
within six months from the date of the licensing decision, under the penalty of having
its license revoked.
2. Due to exceptional or unexpected circumstances, this deadline may be extended for
additional periods of six (6) months at most, upon a justified request, to be settled by
the Central Council.
Article 16 - Cessation of Operations:
If the Institution ceases its operations for a period of six consecutive months, its license shall
be revoked.
9

Part III
General Ongoing Requirements for all Categories of Electronic Payment Services
Providers
Article 17 - General Requirements for Business Continuity:
1. The Institution must notify the BDL and the BCCL of any changes to the services
provided that may lead to a modification in the way these are provided to customers
(adding new features, etc.). The BDL and the BCCL shall each have the right to
object to these changes.
2. The Institution must comply with the submitted business plan that shall be assessed
every 6 months, particularly in terms of securing the number of users and operations
proposed in this plan, under penalty of having its license revoked.
3. The Institution is prohibited from issuing, and/or dealing, and/or facilitating dealings
in virtual assets in any way, unless as authorized by regulations issued by the BDL in
this regard.
4. The Institution is prohibited from issuing debenture bonds.
5. The Institution is prohibited from engaging in any activity that violates the applicable
laws or the regulations issued by the BDL, such as money exchange, lending, or
trading in virtual assets.
6. The Institution providing services under categories A, B, and C may market prepaid
co-branded bank cards or debit cards to its users, provided that:
a- It obtains the BDL prior approval.
b- It contracts with a bank or financial institution licensed by the BDL to issue such
cards.
c- These cards are issued by the contracted bank or financial institution in the name
of the cardholder.
d- The cardholder is subject to due diligence procedures conducted by the card
issuing bank or financial institution, and the card account movement is monitored
by the issuing bank or financial institution.
e- The card limit does not exceed USD 10,000 (ten thousand U.S. Dollars) or its
equivalent in Lebanese Pound.
7. The Institution may provide salary domiciliation services through the bank card,
provided the domiciliated salary does not exceed the card limit.
8. The Institution providing services under categories A, B, and C must install a camera
in each of its branches and at each of its agents (where applicable) to capture all
operations executed on its behalf. Camera records shall be kept for at least 6 months.
9. The Institution must pay the Banque du Liban an annual fee of LBP 3,000,000,000
(three billion Lebanese Pound) for each category of payment services it is authorized
10

to provide. The fee shall be paid for the first time upon obtaining the license, and
thereafter each year by 31 January, under penalty of having the service-related license
revoked.
10. The Institution must provide the Legal Department with all documents related to its
registration with the Commercial Register Secretariat (Registration certificate,
minutes of meeting of the Constituent Assembly, the first Board minutes of meeting,
the bylaws and related amendments, minutes of meeting relating to the election of the
incumbent Board Chairperson and members and the appointment of the General
Manager and Assistant General Managers, if any, minutes of capital subscription,
minutes of capital increase, and minutes of subscription and increase verification,
etc.).
11. The Institution must undertake to provide the BDL and/or the BCCL with any
contract, record or entry it may request.
Article 18 - Requirements for Regulatory Capital and Capital Reconstitution:
1. The Institution must always ensure that its assets exceed its liabilities toward third
parties by an amount at least equal to its regulatory capital (formed of capital shares,
capital allocations, legal and statutory reserves, retained earnings, financial cycle
results, profit and loss statement).
2. Upon its capital increase, the Institution must complete all the capital increase
procedures within a maximum period of three (3) months from the date of the BDL
approval thereon.
3. If, at the end of a financial cycle, the value of the Institution’s own funds falls below
the minimum capital requirement according to the periodic financial statements sent
to the BDL and the BCCL, the Institution must reconstitute its capital through cash
injection by shareholders within three (3) months from the impairment date, under
penalty of having its license revoked.
Article 19 - Governance Requirements:
1. The Board of Directors must approve the overall strategy and the internal control
framework, including policies and procedures related to the Institution’s work. It shall
also be responsible for understanding the risks to which the Institution is exposed,
closely monitoring the management’s work, with active supervision of the
management to ensure that it is performing all its duties.
2. The Board of Directors may establish, according to the Institution’s size and services,
the committees needed to assist it in its duties. These committees shall be formed of
members chosen among the Board of Directors.
3. The Board of Directors must appoint officers responsible for internal audit, risk
management, and compliance, provided that they have the necessary academic and
11

technical knowledge, as well as the experience required to occupy these positions.
The BDL and the BCCL shall be notified of the names and CVs of the persons
appointed, and of any changes thereto upon their occurence. The Institution must
comply with any objection to the persons assigned to these positions.
4. The Institution must promptly notify the BDL and the BCCL, in detail, of any lawsuit
initiated against it, its shareholders, or its managers, upon their occurrence.
Article 20 - Internal Control Requirements:
The Institution must continuously maintain an effective internal control framework (covering
branches and agents, where applicable) that is appropriate to the services it provides and the
volume of its operations, as per Basic Decision No. 7737 of 15 December 2000 (Internal
Control and Internal Audit).
Article 21 - Risk Management Requirements:
1. The Risk Management Unit (or Risk Officer) must be independent from the
Institution’s daily operations, and must report administratively to the General
Manager, provided it directly communicates with the Board of Directors.
2. The Risk Management Unit (or Risk Officer) must be in charge of identifying the
risks to which the Institution, its branches, and its agents (where applicable) are
exposed, of measuring those risks and controlling them, and reporting them through
documented reports submitted periodically and as needed to the Board of Directors,
with a copy to the General Manager.
Article 22 - Internal Audit Requirements:
1. The Internal Audit Unit (or Internal Auditor) must be independent from the
Institution’s daily operations, and must report directly to the Board of Directors.
2. The Internal Audit Unit (or Internal Auditor) must conduct an independent assessment
of the internal control and risk management policies and procedures in place, and also
the extent of compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and with internal
policies and procedures, at the level of the Institution, its branches and its agents.
3. The Internal Audit Unit (or Internal Auditor) must submit its report periodically and
as needed, directly to the Board of Directors, with a copy to the General Manager and
other concerned administrative parties.
Article 23 - External Audit Requirements:
1. The Institution must enter into contract with an Independent Auditor who shall meet
at least the requirements stipulated in Decree No. 1983 of 25 September 1971, and
who shall be affiliated with a foreign audit institution with extensive and specialized
experience in financial audit and IT Audit.
12

2. The Independent Auditor must prepare the following:
a- An annual report on the Institution’s financial statements, with all the
necessary attachments (Independent Auditor’s Report on the Financial
Statements).
b- An annual report on the compliance of the Institution, its branches, and its
agents, with applicable laws and regulations.
c- An annual report on the AML/CFT procedures at the Institution, its branches,
and its agents, as per the requirements of Basic Decision No. 7818 of 18 May
2001 and Basic Decision No. 13769 of 14 November 2025.
d- An annual report on the Institution’s electronic operations and its technical
and organizational status with respect to these operations, including
information on the technical and organizational status at its branches and
agents.
3. The Institution must send copies of these reports to the BDL and the BCCL by 30
April of each year.
4. The BDL Central Council and the BCCL are entitled to object to the appointment of
the Independent Auditor, and this objection shall be binding on the Institution.
Article 24 - IT Infrastructure and Information Security:
The Institution must comply, where applicable, with the regulatory rules on IT security and
with the provisions of Basic Decision No. 10227 of 21 August 2009 (Business Continuity
Plan) and Basic Decision No. 12725 of 28 November 2017 (Cybercrime Prevention).
Article 25 - Electronic Signature (E-signature):
In order to adopt the e-signature, the following conditions must be met concurrently:
1. The customer’s consent is obtained regarding the likely risks associated with the e-
signature.
2. Appropriate measures are taken to ensure utmost security, on the full responsibility of
concerned parties.
3. The e-signature is uniquely linked to the signatory, and is organized and stored in a
way to ensure its authenticity and the integrity of the customer’s personal data.
4. The e-signature is capable of identifying the signatory.
5. The e-signature is created by using e-signature creation data that the signatory can,
with a high level of confidence, use under his/her sole control.
6. The e-signature is linked to the data signed so that any subsequent change in the data
is detectable.
7. The one-time password (OTP) serves as the customer’s e-signature.
13

Article 26 - Electronic Know Your Customer (E-KYC) Form:
1. To adopt the E-KYC Form, the Institution must obtain prior approval from the BDL
for onboarding new customers that are natural persons through the E-KYC Form
(Annex 7), in order to open Payment Accounts whose value do not exceed USD
10,000 and/or to execute financial operations within this limit, as the case may be.
2. The BDL must be provided with documents related to the technologies, mechanisms,
and software to be used for adopting the E-KYC Form. The approval request must
evidence that the Institution:
a- Complies with applicable laws and regulations, particularly those related to
compliance and AML/CFT, especially in terms of:
 Identifying and verifying the customer's identity, through:
- The implementation of enhanced due diligence.
- The adoption of Digital ID Systems that include the requirements for
identity proofing and enrolment and for the identity authentication
and lifecycle management, as per FATF Guidance on Digital ID.
- The adoption of facial recognition systems that are linked to the photo
on the user’s identification document.
 Ongoing monitoring of electronic operations, as per adopted standards,
including those specified in Basic Decision No. 7818 of 18 May 2001.
Setting also system controls that prevent operations from being executed
outside the policies adopted by the Institution and the Circulars issued by
the BDL and the BCCL.
 Adopting a mechanism for customers’ classification based on their risk
categories (high, medium, and low risk) and the risk categories that may
arise from operations ceilings.
b- Ensures that the conditions for the e-signature specified in this Decision are
met.
c- Adopts appropriate safety and compliance measures that ensure utmost legal
and technical protection, particularly in light of the customer risk and the
risks associated with their operations ceilings.
3. The Institution adopting the E-KYC Form must immediately notify the customer of
the details of the performed operation, upon its execution, through an In-App
notification, and/or e-mail, and/or SMS sent to their mobile.
4. The Institution adopting the E-KYC Form must provide the customer, electronically,
with a detailed monthly statement of all the executed operations, when needed.
14

Article 27 - Data Hosting Requirements:
The Institution must store in Lebanon all data and information pertaining to customers and
executed operations (Local Data Hosting).
Article 28 - Insurance Requirements:
1. The Institution must contract with a leading licensed Lebanese insurance company
that reinsures its operations with “A” rated international insurance companies, in
order to cover the operations it conducts and all risks it may face (cyber risks, theft,
breach of trust, cyber hacking, etc.).
2. The Institution must provide the BDL and the BCCL with the insurance contracts
signed, within one month from its licensing date by the BDL, under penalty of having
its license revoked.
3. The Institution must review the insurance contracts on an annual basis, and
immediately provide the BDL and the BCCL with any amendments thereto, under
penalty of having its license revoked.
Article 29 - Customer Protection:
1. The Institution is prohibited from receiving deposits under Article 125 of the Code of
Money and Credit or from marketing to attract deposits.
2. The Institution must state, in the terms and conditions on using an electronic
application and/or website, that any accounts opened are payment accounts.
3. The Institution must comply, where applicable, with the rules on conducting financial
operations with customers, as mentioned in Basic Decision No. 11947 of 12 February
2015, particularly in terms of:
a- Posting clearly on the Institution’s website and electronic application, all
commissions and fees it collects for any type of operation or service it
provides.
b- Publishing a summary of the key facts statements regarding the
services/products provided.
c- Preparing and posting, on the website and electronic application, a clear
mechanism for receiving, reviewing, and deciding on customers’ claims
(complaints), and notifying customers of the outcome of the claim processing
within 15 days at most from the date on which the claim was received.
Article 30 - Personal Data Protection:
The Institution must apply personal data protection measures, in particular those specified in
Annex (3) of this Decision.
15

16

Article 31 - Outsourcing:
1. The Institution is prohibited from outsourcing risk management, compliance, and
internal audit, to a third party.
2. This prohibition shall not apply to functions related to IT security, cyber risk
management, and internal audit of IT and IT security, provided that:
a- A prior approval is obtained from the BDL.
b- The outsourcing is subject to the supervision of the BCCL.
Article 32 - Head Office and Branches:
1. The Institution providing services under categories A, B, C, and D must open a head
office and communicate its address to the BDL and the BCCL, and promptly notify
them of any change in that address.
2. The Institution providing services under categories A, B, C, and D may open
branches, provided they communicate their number and addresses to the BDL and the
BCCL, and promptly notify them of any change thereto.
3. The Institution must allocate an amount of LBP 2,000,000,000 (two billion Lebanese
pound) for each branch.
4. The Institution must comply with any request to close a branch if it does not abide by
the working rules specified in this Decision.
Article 33 - Agents:
1. The Institution providing services under categories A, B, C, and D may contract with
agents from among the institutions duly registered in the Commercial Register.
2. The Institution may contract, across all governorates (Mohafazat), with a maximum
number of 1,200 agents.
3. The Institution may not contract with agents in a specific governorate, unless it has
already opened one branch at least in that governorate, and provided that the number
of agents per branch does not exceed 30 agents. Each branch shall be responsible for
controlling and monitoring the activities of its affiliated agents.
4. The Institution must regularize the relationship with the agent pursuant to a contract
signed by both parties. This contract shall include working rules in line with the
provisions of this Decision, the authorized and prohibited activities, the method for
recording and storing data and evidencing documents, and the reports to be prepared
by the agent for the Institution.
5. When contracting with an agent, the Institution must communicate to the BDL and the
BCCL:
a- The name and address of the agent.
b- The services provided by the agent.
17

c- The names of the persons who shall provide services at the agent.
d- The number and address of the agents, and any changes in this information upon
occurrence.
6. The Institution must allocate a unique identification code or number for each agent,
and must post the list of agents on its electronic website and application.
7. The Institution must allocate, out of its capital, an amount of LBP 1,000,000,000 (one
billion Lebanese pound) for each agent with whom a contract is made.
8. The Institution must comply with any objection regarding any of its agents, under
penalty of having its license revoked.
9. The Institution must conduct an annual internal audit on the agents’ activities.
10. The account balance between the Institution and its agents must be covered by a cash
guarantee or a bank guarantee in favor of the Institution, and the agent may not
override the guarantee limit.
11. The Institution must periodically verify and scrutinize, on its full responsibility, that:
a- The persons responsible at the agent comply with the Fit and Proper criteria,
where applicable.
b- The agent has periodically updated policies, procedures, and regulations that
ensure AML/CFT due diligence procedures.
c- The agents do not engage in any activity that violates applicable laws and the
regulations issued by the BDL, such as exchange or lending or trading in virtual
assets.
12. The Institution shall prepare reports, at least annually and as needed, on the
aforementioned Subparagraphs, including obtaining from agents evidence on their
compliance with the requirements above. These reports and evidencing documents
shall be available for the BCCL’s controllers, upon their request.
13. The Institution must cease working with any agent that do not comply with the
working conditions and rules set forth in this Decision.
Article 34 - Automated Teller Machines (ATMs):
After obtaining the BDL prior approval, the Institution providing services under categories A,
B, and C, may install ATMs for funds withdrawal and deposit, provided that:
1. These ATMs meet all safety standards that ensure the necessary protection for users,
and comply with any requirement imposed by the BDL for this purpose.
2. The number of ATMs outside the Institution’s branches does not exceed the number
of its branches plus its head office. This number shall not include ATMs installed and
operated at the Institution’s branches and head office, regardless of their number.
18

Part IV
Ongoing Working Conditions Specific to Each Category of Electronic Payment Services
Article 35 - Conditions for Category A (E-Money service):
First: Operations ceilings
1. The Institution must enable the customer to deposit funds into, and withdraw funds from
the E-Wallet (Cash in – Cash out) as follows:
a- In cash, at any of its branches, agents or contracted banks, or through
withdrawal/deposit ATMs;
b- and/or through the use of bank cards;
c- and/or through bank accounts; and/or
d- and/or through another E-Wallet, after obtaining the BDL approval to use
this method if the wallet belongs to the customer of another institution.
2. The total balance of the wallet in Lebanese pound and foreign currencies must not
exceed, at any time, the ceilings specified below:
a- For natural persons: USD 3,000 or its equivalent in Lebanese pound.
b- For commercial companies/institutions registered in the Commercial
Register: USD 30,000 (thirty thousand US dollars) or its equivalent in
Lebanese pound.
c- For self-employed professionals affiliated with a specific syndicate:
USD 30,000 or its equivalent in Lebanese pound.
3. In addition to the foregoing, the total amount of funds transferred in Lebanese pound and
foreign currencies to the E-Wallet through all of the means available above, must not
exceed per month the ceilings below:
a- For natural persons: USD 10,000 (ten thousand US dollars) or its
equivalent in Lebanese pound.
b- For commercial companies/institutions registered in the Commercial
Register: USD 50,000 (fifty thousand US dollars) or its equivalent in
Lebanese pound.
c- For self-employed professionals affiliated with a specific syndicate:
USD 50,000 (fifty thousand US dollars) or its equivalent in Lebanese
pound.
4. The total amount transferred to the E-Wallet is non-revolving within a single month.
5. The institution must put in place appropriate IT systems with System Controls to ensure
compliance with the above-mentioned ceilings and prevent any overriding, under penalty
of having its license revoked.
6. For commercial companies registered in the Commercial Register and for self-employed
professionals affiliated with a specific syndicate, the Banque du Liban may exceptionally

approve a ceiling higher than that referred to in Subparagraph (3) above, based on a
request sent by the Institution to the Banque du Liban explaining, at least, the activity of
the companies/self-employed professionals, and the actual volume of their operations that
justifies their need for higher ceilings.
Second: Safeguarding of customers’ funds
1. Regarding the E-Wallets funds belonging to all users, the Institution must
adopt the following mechanism:
a- Open in its name a special and independent bank account in one bank
or more in Lebanon, in order to deposit therein 90% of the E-Wallets
funds belonging to users.
b- Create a credit operation at each concerned bank referred to in Clause
(a) above, whereby 50% of the account opened at that bank is
transferred to a special, independent, and non-interest-bearing account
opened specifically for this purpose at the BDL in the name of the
concerned bank.
c- Keep in cash 10% at most of the E-Wallet funds belonging to users.
2. The concerned institution must verify on a monthly basis that the funds
deposited with the BDL represent the required 50% ratio, in a way to cover
any shortfall in this ratio, and it may also withdraw any excess. The concerned
institution may, at its own responsibility, in the event of insufficient liquidity
or unexpected circumstances, not comply with this percentage and use these
funds exclusively to repay to users the balances of e-wallets.
3. The concerned institution must communicate to the BDL and the BCCL the
names of banks where the E-Wallet funds were deposited.
4. The Institution must maintain at all times in its accounts with banks (i.e. the
Banque du Liban and commercial banks) or in cash at the concerned
institution and its branches and agents, a ratio of at least 100% of the accounts
in the E-Wallets. The institution must submit to the BDL and the BCCL a
monthly statement signed by the General Manager and the internal audit
manager of the concerned institution, detailing its assets and liabilities and the
extent of its compliance with the ratio above.
5. The concerned institution is prohibited from using the E-Wallet funds for any
other purpose (lending, financing, expenses...) than paying the E-Wallet
balances to their users. These funds must always be free of any restrictions.
Third: Other conditions
1. The Institution must conduct enhanced due diligence toward its customers
(onboarding customers).

2. The Institution must classify e-wallets users according to their risk level and
must monitor all executed transfers and payments. It must also conduct
focused inquiry and investigation on any user who carries out periodic
transactions, and immediately freeze the use of the E-wallet if it suspects that
the user is carrying out suspicious transactions, and report the matter to the
SIC.
3. The Institution must comply with the AML/CFT procedures that are specified
as per the FATF recommendations and mentioned in Annex (6).
4. The Institution must not collect a commission above 0.5% of the value of each
operation conducted through the E-Wallet for person-to-person (P2P)
operations.
5. The Institution may perform an exchange operation on cash funds deposited in
the E-Wallet, provided that it has contracted for that purpose with a bank or a
category “A” exchange institution, and that it has obtained prior approval from
the Banque du Liban to provide this service.
6. The Institution may provide salary domiciliation service through the E-Wallet,
provided that the domiciliated salary does not exceed the E-Wallet’s monthly
ceiling.
7. The Institution is prohibited from allowing its customers to open bank
accounts and/or make any investments, and/or benefit from loans granted by
banks or financial institutions. All previous approvals granted in this respect
shall be automatically repealed.
8. The Institution must:
a- Link the E-Wallet to a phone number registered in the name of the
concerned user if he/she is a natural person, or to the user’s email if the
user is a legal person.
b- Send a notification to the user immediately after they perform any
operation on the E-Wallet.
c- Give the user the ability to:
- Reject any operation to receive funds, before adding the amount to
the user’s balance, and provided that the unapproved funds are
automatically returned to the source.
- Completely block any other user.
d- Ensure that operations are executed in real time.
9. The Institution is prohibited from displaying on the E-Wallet, automatically
and without the concerned user’s explicit prior consent, the name of that user
to other users listed in the user’s phone contacts. This consent shall be
obtained by sending a specific message in this regard (pop-up message, email,
SMS).

wallet under the penalty of its closure, provided that this communication is

If the user does not respond and the Institution closes the wallet, the customer

b- Execute the transfer in real time, so that the full amount is transferred

transferred amount was not received by the recipient 90 days after the date of

Part V
Fines, Administrative Sanctions, and Prosecutions
Article 40 - Fines:
The Central Council may determine and impose a fine not exceeding 1,500,000,000 LBP
(one billion five hundred million Lebanese pound) for each violation of the provisions of this
Decision, and of the relevant Statements imposed by this Decision.
Article 41 - Administrative Sanctions:
In addition to the foregoing, and whether the institution violates its bylaws, the provisions of
this Decision, or the measures imposed, or provides incomplete or inaccurate information or
data, the BDL may refer it to the Higher Banking Commission to impose the following
administrative sanctions to the infringing institution:
1. A warning.
2. Forbid the institution to carry out some operations, or impose any other limitations
on the institution’s activities or services.
3. Forbid the Board Chairperson and/or members, and/or General Managers to
conduct the operations covered by this Decision, for good or for a limited period.
4. Revoke its license.
Article 42 - Prosecution:
The violation of the provisions of this Basic Decision constitutes an offense under Article 770
of the Penal Code, and the BDL may prosecute any infringing institution before the
competent judicial authority.
Article 43 - The Role of the Banking Control Commission of Lebanon:
The BCCL shall monitor the sound implementation of the provisions of this Decision, and
shall issue implementation texts when necessary.
Article 44 - Transitional Provisions:
1. Non-banking institutions previously licensed by the BDL as per the provisions of
Basic Decision No. 7548 of 30 March 2000 (Electronic Financial and Banking
Operations), shall be automatically governed by the provisions of this Decision.
2. Non-banking institutions previously licensed by the BDL shall be granted, based on
Basic Decision No. 7548 of 30 March 2000, a six-month time limit to comply with
the provisions of this Decision, particularly to obtain the necessary licenses and abide
by the submitted business plan. Failure to do so will result in the revocation of the
license granted in relation to the service provided.

3. Submission to the BDL of licensing requests to provide any of the services in
aforementioned categories A, B, C, and D, shall be suspended until further notice.
Article 45 - List of Electronic Payment Services Providers:
The Banque du Liban shall publish annually in the Official Gazette in the month of January,
the list of Electronic Payment Services Providers, and shall also publish in the Official
Gazette any amendment to that list.
Article 46 - Entry into force of this Decision:
This Decision shall enter into force upon its issuance.
Article 47 - Publication:
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.

Part 1:
First: For the purpose of implementing the provisions of this Article, the following
expressions shall mean:
- Customer: Any natural or legal person, whether a company or an institution of
any type, or any legal arrangement (e.g. a trust), or any body, organization or
non-profit organization (mutual funds, cooperatives, welfare centers,
charities, clubs, etc.).
- Beneficial Owner: Any natural person who ultimately owns or exercises
ultimate effective control, whether directly or indirectly, over the customer
and/or the natural person on whose behalf operations are carried out.
Indirect ownership and/or control shall include the situations where the
ownership and/or control is exercised through a chain of ownership or by
means of control other than direct control.
Second: Any institution providing the E-money service, the local money transfer service,
and the cross-border money transfer service, must comply, at least, with the
following:
1. To apply due diligence procedures to customers and beneficial owners,
regardless of the operation's value, which include verifying the identity of both
permanent and occasional customers, whether resident or non-resident;
determining the nature of their business; understanding the ownership structure
and/or control over the legal entity; understanding and identifying the purpose
and nature of the business relationship; obtaining data on that purpose when
necessary; identifying the beneficial owner and the source of funds; and
conducting ongoing monitoring of operations, particularly in the following
cases:
a- Before or when a business relationship is being established or started.
b- When carrying out a single operation or several linked operations whose
total is equal to, or above, USD 10,000 or its equivalent.
c- Whenever a customer is suspected to attempt a money laundering or
terrorist financing operation.
2. To apply due diligence procedures to existing customers based on materiality
and risk, and to conduct due diligence on such existing business relationships
in a timely manner, considering whether and when these measures have
previously been taken, and the adequacy of the data obtained.

First: When multiple cross-border electronic transfers from a single originator are bundled

transfers must:

electronic transfer.
- Take reasonable measures to identify electronic transfers that lack required
originator or beneficiary information. Such measures should be consistent with
straight-through processing.
- Have risk-based policies and procedures in place for determining when to
execute, reject, or suspend such electronic transfers, as well as appropriate
follow-up actions.
Where technical limitations prevent the required originator or beneficiary
information accompanying a cross-border electronic transfer from being kept
with a related domestic electronic transfer, the intermediary institution should
keep, for at least five years, all the information received from the originating
